svg.title: Hubbard rectangular: the best energies at each size
svg.desc: periodic, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 32 energies at 2 sizes, sizes 32, 64; periodic, 6 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 12 energies at 4 sizes, sizes 96, 192, 288, 384; periodic, 8 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 6 energies at 3 sizes, sizes 128, 192, 256; periodic/open, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 9 energies at 2 sizes, sizes 32, 64
svg.text: Hubbard rectangular: the best energies at each size
4 Hamiltonians, one panel per set of couplings, at every size with a published result. Each size is placed against its exact energy
where it has one (sizes in grey), otherwise against the standing record (sizes in orange), whose holder then sits in the band
above the plot. One line per method family through its best energy at each size; a better energy is higher.
Below the energy it is measured against
periodic, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 32 energies at 2 sizes
periodic, 6 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 12 energies at 4 sizes
periodic, 8 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 6 energies at 3 sizes
periodic/open, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 9 energies at 2 sizes
Sizes are numbers of sites. A family's line joins its best energy at each size, whichever paper set it, so a line is a family's reach rather than
one calculation. Where the reference is the record, the heights say how far behind the others are and nothing about the record itself.
